claims.text: In-situ TEM and XRD can optimize the microstructure and properties of RHEAs.
In-situ characterization can enable a large-scale reaction and a stable microstructure in a refractory-alloy/Cu system.
The material initially consists of individual refractory alloying elements and Cu.
The proposed intervention is the use of in-situ characterization techniques.
RHEAs are relevant for high-temperature conditions.
RHEAs possess irradiation resistance suitable for the proposed conditions.
Microstructural evolution and phase transformations are the structural mediators connecting in-situ characterization to performance.
In-situ characterization improves performance by optimizing processing, microstructure, and properties.
The intervention will improve the mechanical strength of RHEAs relative to conventional processing.
The intervention will improve the irradiation resistance of RHEAs relative to conventional processing.
The intervention will improve the thermal stability of RHEAs relative to conventional processing.
RHEAs can exhibit high mechanical strength and stable phase structures at elevated temperatures.
Conventional processing methods provide the comparison baseline.
A significant positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu limits current processing methods.
The exact processing–microstructure–property relationship in RHEAs is not fully understood.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing conventionally processed RHEAs with RHEAs described as processed using in-situ characterization.
Failure to improve strength, irradiation resistance, and thermal stability relative to the conventional-processing control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as characterization, but the experiment treats characterization as a processing method. Observation by in-situ TEM or XRD is not itself a specified synthesis or reaction method.
